title: The Louisiana Purchase: Not a Purchase
summary: Josh and Chuck examine the 1803 Louisiana Purchase and argue it was not a straightforward land purchase. They trace the territory's naming under King Louis XIV, René-Robert Cavelier de La Salle's claim, French and Spanish control, Spain's buffer-zone use, Napoleon's secret return of the territory to France via the Third Treaty of San Ildefonso, Haiti's Saint-Domingue revolution undermining French interest, and the negotiations led by Robert Livingston and James Monroe with Barbé-Marbois and Talleyrand for $15 million. They cover constitutional doubts raised by Jefferson, the Senate ratification, the Doctrine of Discovery as the legal basis for what was transferred, the treaty with the Sac and Fox (Harrison's 1804 treaty), Native removal, Lewis and Clark, and westward expansion through the Gadsden Purchase and the Oregon and Texas acquisitions. The episode closes with a listener mail segment from Tim about the word "Sarah" and a sign-off.

entities.name: René-Robert Cavelier, Sieur de La Salle

segments.title: Opening and setup
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the episode as a myth-busting look at the Louisiana Purchase, then begin the early history of the name Louisiana and La Salle's claim for France.

segments.title: French and Spanish control of Louisiana
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Antoine Crozat's charter, France's transfer of the territory to Spain after the Seven Years War, and Spain's limited settlement and use of Louisiana as a buffer zone.

segments.title: Jefferson, New Orleans access, and Napoleon's secret treaty
segments.summary: Spain revokes American trading rights at New Orleans, and Napoleon secretly regains the territory through the Third Treaty of San Ildefonso in 1800, with Saint-Domingue's economic value a factor.

segments.title: Mid-episode break
segments.summary: Short break before the next section.

segments.title: Haitian Revolution and Napoleon's decision to sell
segments.summary: The Haitian Revolution removes Saint-Domingue's profitability, leading Napoleon to decide to sell the Louisiana territory; the hosts also joke about Napoleon's height.

segments.title: Negotiations and the $15 million price
segments.summary: Livingston and Monroe negotiate with Barbé-Marbois and Talleyrand in Paris, settling at fifteen million dollars for about 828,000 square miles, beyond the ten million authorized for New Orleans, with the deal announced July 4, 1803.

segments.title: Constitutional doubts and Senate ratification
segments.summary: Jefferson worries the purchase is unconstitutional, Gallatin argues the treaty power covers it, the Senate ratifies 24 to 7, and the Supreme Court later upholds the view under John Marshall.

segments.title: Doctrine of Discovery and Native removal
segments.summary: The hosts explain that the purchase transferred the French claim under the Doctrine of Discovery, which shaped treaties with Native nations, including the 1804 Sac and Fox land deal under William Henry Harrison, and later removals culminating in the Trail of Tears; they also cover Manifest Destiny and western expansion via the Gadsden Purchase, Oregon, and Texas.

segments.title: Listener mail and sign-off
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck read listener mail from Tim about the word Sarah and close with the show's sign-off and a promotional note.
